subproblems.title: Continuous functions are integrable on open boxes of Euclid n
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let a, b ∈ ℝ be arbitrary (no order between a and b is assumed). Give ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) its Lebesgue measure, and write z_j for the j-th coordinate. If h : ℝⁿ → ℝ is continuous, then h is Lebesgue integrable on the open box B = {z ∈ ℝⁿ : a < z_j < b for all j ∈ Fin n}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), Continuous h → IntegrableOn h {z : Euclid n | ∀ j, a < z j ∧ z j < b}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F3) of the parent proof of `cmcdt_cbm_smooth_trace`: continuous functions are bounded on the closed cube, which has finite measure, so all integrals over Q_δ are finite. Here it is isolated as a lemma about an arbitrary open box. The parent uses it for the integrands ∂_i(vG_i), Dv(G) and ‖Dv‖, and the sibling `cmcdt_cbm_st_coord_bound` uses it for F, H, |v| and ‖Dv‖.

Notation. n ∈ ℕ. ℝⁿ is `Euclid n` = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure (volume), and z_j := z.ofLp j is the j-th coordinate (j ∈ Fin n). Let a, b ∈ ℝ be arbitrary; no order between them is assumed. Put B := {z ∈ ℝⁿ : a < z_j < b for all j}. Let h : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous. Claim: h is integrable on B (IntegrableOn h B).

1. Closed box. Let I := {w ∈ Fin n → ℝ : a ≤ w_j ≤ b for all j}. This is the order interval Icc (fun _ => a) (fun _ => b) for the product order. Let K := toLp(I) ⊆ ℝⁿ be its image under the canonical map toLp 2 : (Fin n → ℝ) → Euclid n. (If a > b and n ≥ 1, then I = K = ∅. If n = 0, then I and K are single points. Neither case needs separate treatment.)
2. B ⊆ K. Let z ∈ B and w := z.ofLp. Then a < w_j < b, hence a ≤ w_j ≤ b, for every j. So w ∈ I and z = toLp w ∈ K.
3. K is compact. I is compact because closed order intervals of the finite product Fin n → ℝ are compact (Mathlib `isCompact_Icc`). The map toLp 2 is continuous (`PiLp.continuous_toLp`), and the continuous image of a compact set is compact.
4. h is integrable on K. h is continuous, so it is continuous on K. Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is finite on compact sets, so a function continuous on a compact set is integrable on it (`ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact`).
5. Since B ⊆ K (step 2), integrability restricts from K to B (`IntegrableOn.mono_set`). Hence h is integrable on B. ∎

subproblems.title: Coordinate slicing (Fubini) on an open cube of Euclid (m+1)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, i ∈ Fin (m+1) and a ≤ b real. Give ℝ^{m+1} = Euclid (m+1) Lebesgue measure and ℝ^m = (Fin m → ℝ) the product Lebesgue measure. Let h : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ be integrable on Q = {z ∈ ℝ^{m+1} : a < z_j < b for all j}, and let Q' = {y ∈ ℝ^m : a < y_k < b for all k}. For t ∈ ℝ and y ∈ ℝ^m, let ι(t, y) = toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i t y) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}: the point whose i-th coordinate is t and whose remaining coordinates are y_0, …, y_{m−1} in order. Then (I) the function y ↦ ∫_a^b h(ι(t, y)) dt (interval integral) is integrable on Q', and (II) ∫_Q h = ∫_{Q'} (∫_a^b h(ι(t, y)) dt) dy.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (i : Fin (m + 1)) (a b : ℝ) (h : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), a ≤ b → IntegrableOn h {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ j, a < z j ∧ z j < b} → IntegrableOn (fun y : Fin m → ℝ => ∫ t in a..b, h (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i t y))) {y : Fin m → ℝ | ∀ j, a < y j ∧ y j < b} ∧ ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ j, a < z j ∧ z j < b}, h x = ∫ y in {y : Fin m → ℝ | ∀ j, a < y j ∧ y j < b}, ∫ t in a..b, h (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i t y))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F2) of the parent proof of `cmcdt_cbm_smooth_trace`. That fact is Fubini in coordinate i: the map (t, x') ↦ ι_i(t, x') is a measure-preserving bijection ℝ × ℝ^{n−1} → ℝⁿ. It is obtained from Mathlib `MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove` composed with the measure-preserving identification Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ), and it maps (a, b) × Q' onto Q. Here the fact is stated for an arbitrary box (a, b)^{m+1} with a ≤ b. The statement also includes the integrability of the slice function, which the parent's steps 2–4 use implicitly when they integrate inequalities in x'.

Notation. m ∈ ℕ and i ∈ Fin (m+1).
- ℝ^{m+1} := `Euclid (m+1)` with Lebesgue measure, and z_j := z.ofLp j.
- ℝ^m := Fin m → ℝ with its product Lebesgue measure (`volume` = `Measure.pi`). For m = 0 this is a single point of mass 1.
- For t ∈ ℝ and y ∈ ℝ^m, let ι(t, y) := toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i t y) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}. This is the point with i-th coordinate t whose other coordinates are y_0, …, y_{m−1} in increasing order of index: ι(t, y)_i = t and ι(t, y)_{i.succAbove k} = y_k (`Fin.insertNth_apply_same`, `Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove`).
- Q := {z ∈ ℝ^{m+1} : a < z_j < b for all j} and Q' := {y ∈ ℝ^m : a < y_k < b for all k}.

Hypotheses: a ≤ b, and h : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ is integrable on Q. Let S(y) := ∫_a^b h(ι(t, y)) dt be the oriented interval integral.

Claims:
- (I) S is integrable on Q'.
- (II) ∫_Q h = ∫_{Q'} S(y) dy.

1. Coordinate equivalence. Define E : ℝ × ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} by E(t, y) := ι(t, y). Let P_i := MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) i : (Fin (m+1) → ℝ) ≃ᵐ ℝ × ℝ^m, w ↦ (w_i, (w_{i.succAbove k})_k). Its inverse is (t, y) ↦ Fin.insertNth i t y. Then E is the composite of P_i⁻¹ with the measurable equivalence MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 : (Fin (m+1) → ℝ) ≃ᵐ ℝ^{m+1}. So E is a measurable equivalence, in particular a measurable embedding, and E(t, y) = toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i t y) holds definitionally.
2. E is measure preserving from vol_ℝ ⊗ vol_{ℝ^m} to vol_{ℝ^{m+1}}. P_i is measure preserving (`volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove`), hence so is its inverse (`MeasurePreserving.symm`). toLp 2 is measure preserving (`PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp`). Compose the two (`MeasurePreserving.comp`).
3. E⁻¹(Q) = (a, b) × Q'.
   - E(t, y) ∈ Q iff a < (Fin.insertNth i t y)_j < b for every j ∈ Fin (m+1).
   - Every j is either i or i.succAbove k for some k ∈ Fin m (`Fin.forall_iff_succAbove i`).
   - (Fin.insertNth i t y)_i = t and (Fin.insertNth i t y)_{i.succAbove k} = y_k.
   - So the condition reads (a < t < b) ∧ (∀ k, a < y_k < b), i.e. (t, y) ∈ Ioo a b ×ˢ Q'.
4. Integrability on the product.
   - E is a measure-preserving measurable embedding, so h ∘ E is integrable on E⁻¹(Q) for vol ⊗ vol iff h is integrable on Q (`MeasurePreserving.integrableOn_comp_preimage`). The latter is the hypothesis.
   - By step 3 and `Measure.prod_restrict`, (vol ⊗ vol)|_{(a,b) × Q'} = (vol|_{(a,b)}) ⊗ (vol|_{Q'}).
   - So h ∘ E is integrable for μ := (vol|_{(a,b)}) ⊗ (vol|_{Q'}).
5. Change of variables. By `MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb` (E is a measure-preserving measurable embedding), ∫_Q h = ∫_{E⁻¹(Q)} h(E(p)) d(vol ⊗ vol)(p). By step 3 and `Measure.prod_restrict`, this equals ∫ h ∘ E dμ.
6. Fubini, with the outer integral in the second variable. By step 4 and `integral_prod_symm`, ∫ h ∘ E dμ = ∫_{Q'} (∫_{(a,b)} h(E(t, y)) dt) dy. By `Integrable.integral_prod_right`, the function y ↦ ∫_{(a,b)} h(E(t, y)) dt is integrable with respect to vol|_{Q'}.
7. Interval form. Fix y. Since a ≤ b:
   - ∫_a^b h(ι(t, y)) dt = ∫_{(a,b]} h(ι(t, y)) dt (`intervalIntegral.integral_of_le`);
   - this equals ∫_{(a,b)} h(ι(t, y)) dt (`integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo`; {b} is Lebesgue-null).
   So the inner function of step 6 is S at every y. Step 6 then gives (I), and steps 5–6 give (II). ∎

Remarks.
- No measurability of Q or Q' is needed. `Measure.prod_restrict` holds for arbitrary sets of s-finite measures, and `MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb` / `integrableOn_comp_preimage` only need E to be a measurable embedding. Q and Q' are open in any case.
- The degenerate case a = b is covered by the same argument. Then Q = ∅ (m + 1 ≥ 1 coordinates), so ∫_Q h = 0, and either Q' = ∅ (m ≥ 1) or ∫_a^a = 0 (m = 0). Both sides vanish.

  intro m i a b h hab hint
  set Q : Set (Euclid (m + 1)) := {z | ∀ j, a < z j ∧ z j < b} with hQ
  set Q' : Set (Fin m → ℝ) := {y | ∀ j, a < y j ∧ y j < b} with hQ'
  -- `E (t, y) = toLp 2 (insertNth i t y)`: a measure-preserving equivalence `ℝ × ℝ^m ≃ ℝ^{m+1}`

    (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ : Fin (m + 1) => ℝ) i).symm.trans
      (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin (m + 1) → ℝ))

    (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp (Fin (m + 1))).comp
      (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ : Fin (m + 1) => ℝ) i).symm
  have hEapply : ∀ p : ℝ × (Fin m → ℝ), E p = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i p.1 p.2) :=
    fun p => rfl
  have hpre : E ⁻¹' Q = Ioo a b ×ˢ Q' := by
    ext ⟨t, y⟩
    simp only [Set.mem_preimage, hEapply, Q, Q', Set.mem_prod, Set.mem_Ioo, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
    rw [Fin.forall_iff_succAbove i]
    simp
  have hint' : Integrable (fun p => h (E p))
      ((volume.restrict (Ioo a b)).prod (volume.restrict Q')) := by
    rw [Measure.prod_restrict, ← hpre]
    exact (hE.integrableOn_comp_preimage E.measurableEmbedding).2 hint
  have hinner : ∀ y : Fin m → ℝ, ∫ t in Ioo a b, h (E (t, y)) =

    intro y
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hab, integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo]
    rfl

subproblems.title: One-dimensional boundary-term and trace estimate on an interval
subproblems.statement: Let a < b be real and let φ, γ : ℝ → ℝ be C¹ functions with |γ(t)| ≤ 1 for all t. Then |∫_a^b (φγ)'(t) dt| ≤ (2/(b − a)) ∫_a^b |φ(t)| dt + 2 ∫_a^b |φ'(t)| dt, where ' denotes the derivative (deriv) and the integrals are interval integrals.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (φ γ : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → (∀ t, |γ t| ≤ 1) → a < b → |∫ t in a..b, deriv (fun s => φ s * γ s) t| ≤ 2 / (b - a) * (∫ t in a..b, |φ t|) + 2 * ∫ t in a..b, |deriv φ t|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the one-dimensional core of steps 2–4 of the parent proof of `cmcdt_cbm_smooth_trace`, on a single coordinate line:
- the fundamental theorem of calculus of step 2 for the boundary term H_i = vG_i;
- the bound |H_i| ≤ |v||G| ≤ |v| of step 3;
- the face (trace) estimate of step 4: FTC along the segment between c and t, then averaging over t in a side of length s = b − a.
It is the elementary one-dimensional case of the trace estimate behind Simon, Ch. 2, 2.8–2.9 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 663–676). For background, the BV trace theory is in Evans–Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, Ch. 5. The argument below is self-contained.

Statement. Let a < b and let φ, γ : ℝ → ℝ be C¹ (`ContDiff ℝ 1`) with |γ(t)| ≤ 1 for all t. Write f' := deriv f. All integrals are interval integrals ∫_a^b; since a < b these are ordinary integrals over (a, b]. Claim: |∫_a^b (φγ)'(t) dt| ≤ (2/(b − a)) ∫_a^b |φ| + 2 ∫_a^b |φ'|.

1. FTC for the product. φγ is C¹ as a product of C¹ functions. So it is differentiable everywhere, and its derivative (φγ)' is continuous, hence interval integrable on [a, b]. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (`intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub`), ∫_a^b (φγ)' = φ(b)γ(b) − φ(a)γ(a).
2. Pointwise trace inequality. Put D := ∫_a^b |φ'|. Claim: for every c ∈ [a, b], |φ(c)| ≤ (b − a)⁻¹ ∫_a^b |φ| + D.
   2a. Fix t ∈ [a, b]. φ is differentiable with continuous derivative φ', so by FTC, φ(c) − φ(t) = ∫_t^c φ'. Also |∫_t^c φ'| ≤ |∫_t^c |φ'|| (`intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_abs_integral_norm`). Next, |∫_t^c |φ'|| ≤ D:
       - If t ≤ c, then ∫_t^c |φ'| ≥ 0, and ∫_t^c |φ'| ≤ ∫_a^b |φ'| = D. This holds because a ≤ t ≤ c ≤ b, |φ'| ≥ 0, and |φ'| is continuous, hence interval integrable on [a, b] (`intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval`).
       - If c < t, then ∫_t^c |φ'| = −∫_c^t |φ'| (`intervalIntegral.integral_symm`). The same argument with a ≤ c ≤ t ≤ b gives |∫_t^c |φ'|| = ∫_c^t |φ'| ≤ D.
       Hence |φ(c) − φ(t)| ≤ D, and |φ(c)| ≤ |φ(t)| + |φ(c) − φ(t)| ≤ |φ(t)| + D.

subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n = m + 1, 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4, and Q_δ = {z ∈ ℝⁿ : δ < z_j < 1 − δ for all j} ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). Let i ∈ Fin n and let e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 be the i-th standard unit vector. For all C¹ functions v, g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y: |∫_{Q_δ} D(vg)(x)e_i dx| ≤ 4 ∫_{Q_δ} |v| + 2 ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv‖, where D denotes the Fréchet derivative (fderiv) and ‖Dv(x)‖ its operator norm.

Notation and hypotheses.
- m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. ℝⁿ := `Euclid n` (Lebesgue measure), with coordinates z_j := z.ofLp j. ℝ^m := Fin m → ℝ (product Lebesgue measure).
- 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4, a := δ, b := 1 − δ.
- Q := {z ∈ ℝⁿ : δ < z_j < 1 − δ for all j} and Q' := {y ∈ ℝ^m : δ < y_k < 1 − δ for all k}.
- i ∈ Fin n and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, the i-th standard unit vector (‖e_i‖ = 1, `PiLp.norm_single`).
- ι(t, y) := toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i t y) for t ∈ ℝ, y ∈ ℝ^m.
- v, g : ℝⁿ → ℝ are C¹ (`ContDiff ℝ 1`), and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Claim: |∫_Q D(vg)(x)e_i dx| ≤ 4 ∫_Q |v| + 2 ∫_Q ‖Dv‖, where D(vg)(x)e_i = fderiv ℝ (fun y => v y * g y) x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1).

Sibling lemmas used:
- `cmcdt_cbm_st_box_integrableOn`: continuous functions are integrable on boxes {a < z_j < b}.
- `cmcdt_cbm_st_slice_integral`: for a ≤ b and h integrable on the box, y ↦ ∫_a^b h(ι(t, y)) dt is integrable on Q', and ∫_Q h = ∫_{Q'} ∫_a^b h(ι(t, y)) dt dy.
- `cmcdt_cbm_st_interval_bound`: for a < b, C¹ φ, γ with |γ| ≤ 1, |∫_a^b (φγ)'| ≤ (2/(b − a)) ∫_a^b |φ| + 2 ∫_a^b |φ'|.

0. Since δ ≤ 1/4, b − a = 1 − 2δ ≥ 1/2 > 0. So a < b (in particular a ≤ b) and 2/(b − a) ≤ 4. The hypothesis 0 ≤ δ is carried only to match the parent's hypotheses; this lemma does not use it.
1. Lines. For all t and y, ι(t, y) = ι(0, y) + t·e_i. Check coordinatewise, splitting j ∈ Fin n into j = i and j = i.succAbove k (`Fin.succAboveCases`):
   - at i: t = 0 + t·1;
   - at i.succAbove k ≠ i: y_k = y_k + t·0.
   Hence, for fixed y, t ↦ ι(t, y) is affine, C¹, with derivative e_i at every t (`HasDerivAt` of t ↦ c + t·e_i).
2. Integrands.
   - vg is C¹ (product), so x ↦ D(vg)(x) is continuous, and F(x) := D(vg)(x)e_i is continuous.
   - |v| and ‖Dv‖ are continuous because v is C¹, so H(x) := 4|v(x)| + 2‖Dv(x)‖ is continuous.
   - By `cmcdt_cbm_st_box_integrableOn` with box parameters δ and 1 − δ, the functions F, H, |v| and ‖Dv‖ are integrable on Q.
3. Slicing (`cmcdt_cbm_st_slice_integral`, valid since a ≤ b).
   - Applied to F: ∫_Q F = ∫_{Q'} (∫_a^b F(ι(t, y)) dt) dy.
   - Applied to H: K(y) := ∫_a^b H(ι(t, y)) dt is integrable on Q', and ∫_Q H = ∫_{Q'} K.
4. Linearity on Q. By the integrability of step 2, ∫_Q H = 4 ∫_Q |v| + 2 ∫_Q ‖Dv‖.
5. Line estimate: for every y ∈ ℝ^m, |∫_a^b F(ι(t, y)) dt| ≤ K(y).
   5a. φ(t) := v(ι(t, y)) and γ(t) := g(ι(t, y)) are C¹ (C¹ functions composed with the affine map of step 1), and |γ| ≤ 1.
   5b. By the chain rule (`HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt`) with step 1, for every t: (φγ)'(t) = D(vg)(ι(t, y))e_i = F(ι(t, y)) and φ'(t) = Dv(ι(t, y))e_i.
   5c. By `cmcdt_cbm_st_interval_bound` (a < b) and 5b: |∫_a^b F(ι(t, y)) dt| ≤ (2/(b − a)) ∫_a^b |φ| + 2 ∫_a^b |Dv(ι(t, y))e_i| dt.
   5d. Two comparisons:
       - ∫_a^b |φ| ≥ 0 (a ≤ b, nonnegative integrand) and 2/(b − a) ≤ 4, so (2/(b − a)) ∫_a^b |φ| ≤ 4 ∫_a^b |φ|.
       - For every x, |Dv(x)e_i| ≤ ‖Dv(x)‖·‖e_i‖ = ‖Dv(x)‖ by the operator-norm bound (`ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm`). Both integrands are continuous in t, so monotonicity of the interval integral (a ≤ b) gives ∫_a^b |Dv(ι(t, y))e_i| dt ≤ ∫_a^b ‖Dv(ι(t, y))‖ dt.
   5e. Continuous integrands are interval integrable, so by linearity K(y) = 4 ∫_a^b |φ| + 2 ∫_a^b ‖Dv(ι(t, y))‖ dt. Combining 5c–5e gives the line estimate.
6. Conclusion.
   - |∫_Q F| = |∫_{Q'} ∫_a^b F(ι(t, y)) dt dy| by step 3.
   - This is ≤ ∫_{Q'} |∫_a^b F(ι(t, y)) dt| dy, since |∫f| ≤ ∫|f|.
   - This is ≤ ∫_{Q'} K by monotonicity (`integral_mono_of_nonneg`): the left integrand is ≥ 0, K is integrable on Q' (step 3), and the pointwise bound is step 5.
   - ∫_{Q'} K = ∫_Q H by step 3, and ∫_Q H = 4 ∫_Q |v| + 2 ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ by step 4. ∎

subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and ℝⁿ = Euclid (m+1). Let e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin (m+1)) be the standard basis, and write G_i(y) = (G y)_i for the coordinates of G. If v : ℝⁿ → ℝ and G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ are differentiable at the point x, then v(x)·trace DG(x) = Σ_i D(vG_i)(x)e_i − Dv(x)(G(x)).

Source: step 1 of the parent proof of `cmcdt_cbm_smooth_trace` (product rule for H := vG: ∂_iH_i = (∂_i v)G_i + v ∂_iG_i) together with fact (F1) (div G = trace DG = Σ_i ⟨e_i, DG e_i⟩ = Σ_i ∂_iG_i, via `LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner`). It is stated at a single point and assumes only differentiability at that point.

Notation.
- m ∈ ℕ and ℝⁿ := `Euclid (m+1)`. w_i := w.ofLp i is the i-th coordinate (i ∈ Fin (m+1)).
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. These are the vectors of the standard orthonormal basis `EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m+1)) ℝ` (`EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply`).
- G_i(y) := (G y)_i.

Hypotheses: v : ℝⁿ → ℝ and G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ are differentiable at the point x. Claim: v(x)·trace DG(x) = Σ_i D(vG_i)(x)e_i − Dv(x)(G(x)). Here trace DG(x) = `LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m+1)) (fderiv ℝ G x)` and D(vG_i)(x)e_i = `fderiv ℝ (fun y => v y * G y i) x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)`.

1. Coordinates. G_i = π_i ∘ G, where π_i := EuclideanSpace.proj i : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ, w ↦ w_i, is continuous linear. By the chain rule (π_i is its own derivative), G_i has derivative π_i ∘ DG(x) at x. In particular DG_i(x)e_i = (DG(x)e_i)_i.
2. Product rule at x. v and G_i are differentiable at x, so D(vG_i)(x) = v(x)·DG_i(x) + G_i(x)·Dv(x) (`HasFDerivAt.mul`). Evaluating at e_i: D(vG_i)(x)e_i = v(x)(DG(x)e_i)_i + G_i(x)·Dv(x)e_i.
3. Trace in the standard orthonormal basis. trace DG(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, DG(x)e_i⟩ (`LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner` with `EuclideanSpace.basisFun`). Also ⟨e_i, w⟩ = w_i (`EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left` with coefficient 1). Hence trace DG(x) = Σ_i (DG(x)e_i)_i.
4. Expansion of G(x). G(x) = Σ_i G_i(x)e_i: the j-th coordinate of the right side is Σ_i G_i(x)·[j = i] = G_j(x). Since Dv(x) is linear, Dv(x)(G(x)) = Σ_i G_i(x)·Dv(x)e_i.
5. Sum step 2 over i and use steps 3 and 4: Σ_i D(vG_i)(x)e_i = v(x) Σ_i (DG(x)e_i)_i + Σ_i G_i(x) Dv(x)e_i = v(x)·trace DG(x) + Dv(x)(G(x)). Subtracting Dv(x)(G(x)) from both sides gives the claim. ∎

Without the type ascription, `HasFDerivAt.mul` elaborates the function as the pointwise product `v * fun y => …`, and `rw [h.fderiv]` then fails to match.

```lean
theorem Submission.cmcdt_cbm_st_div_product : ∀ (m : ℕ) (v : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)) (x : Euclid (m + 1)), DifferentiableAt ℝ v x → DifferentiableAt ℝ G x → v x * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G x) = ∑ i, fderiv ℝ (fun y => v y * G y i) x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) - fderiv ℝ v x (G x) := by
  intro m v G x hv hG
  -- derivative of the coordinate `G_i = proj_i ∘ G`
  have hGi : ∀ i : Fin (m + 1), HasFDerivAt (fun y => G y i)
      ((EuclideanSpace.proj i : Euclid (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp (fderiv ℝ G x)) x := fun i =>
    (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Euclid (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).hasFDerivAt.comp x hG.hasFDerivAt
  -- product rule, evaluated at `e_i`
  have hprod : ∀ i : Fin (m + 1),
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => v y * G y i) x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) =
        v x * (fderiv ℝ G x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) i +
          G x i * fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) := by
    intro i
    have h : HasFDerivAt (fun y => v y * G y i)
        (v x • (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Euclid (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp (fderiv ℝ G x) +
          G x i • fderiv ℝ v x) x := hv.hasFDerivAt.mul (hGi i)
    rw [h.fderiv]
    simp
  -- trace in the standard orthonormal basis
  have htrace : LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G x) =
      ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ G x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) i := by
    rw [LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner _ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ)]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left]
    simp
  -- `G x = ∑ i, (G x)_i e_i`, hence `Dv(x)(G x) = ∑ i, (G x)_i ∂_i v(x)`
  have hexp : G x = ∑ i, G x i • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) := by
    ext j
    simp [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.single_apply]
  have hDvG : fderiv ℝ v x (G x) = ∑ i, G x i * fderiv ℝ v x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) := by
    conv_lhs => rw [hexp]
    simp [map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]
  rw [htrace, hDvG, Finset.mul_sum]
  simp only [hprod, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  ring
```
